title: Damaging winds
tldr: Shelter inside a sturdy building away from windows when damaging winds threaten. Avoid trees, power lines and lightweight structures. Follow tornado warnings separately; straight-line winds can also cause severe damage.
steps: Bring loose items inside while conditions are calm; do not go out once winds are dangerous.
Stay away from glass and large exterior openings.
High-profile vehicles are vulnerable; avoid routes lined with falling trees or debris.
Assume downed lines are live and report them from a safe distance.
next: Inspect damage without entering unstable buildings. Arrange help for trees touching wires.
watch: Do not attempt to clear a tree from a power line.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Wait for winds to ease in the best shelter you can reach without exposure. Keep a torch and shoes nearby for broken glass. If the building is failing, move to a safer reachable space without going beneath trees, loose roofing or wires.
household: Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
